rawCommits.subject: feat(video): add video frame thumbnails in sidekick panel
rawCommits.body:
Uses media fragment (#t=0.5) with preload=auto to render a still
frame from the video as the thumbnail. Falls back to Film icon
on error.
rawCommits.cleanSubject: add video frame thumbnails in sidekick panel

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat-app): add ChatGPT-style Chat app at /chat
rawCommits.body:
New top-level app for everyday LLM use. Left panel renders the
date-bucketed sessions list (with search + new-chat) for the user's
super-agent (CEO), main panel mounts the standard ChatPanel /
DesktopChatInputBar against that agent, and the sidekick reuses the
agents-app AgentInfoPanel and is collapsed on first visit. Default
model is seeded to aura-gpt-5-4-mini; user picks still persist via
the existing per-agent localStorage key.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-app): resolve chat agent via setup() so renamed CEOs work
rawCommits.body:
The route was stuck on "Starting chat..." for accounts whose CEO had
been renamed because `useSuperAgent()` requires `name === "ceo" &&
role === "ceo"`. Switch to a one-shot, app-session-cached
`api.superAgent.setup()` call (idempotent server-side) which returns
the canonical chat agent regardless of name/role, and feed it into
the agent store so the sidekick still has Profile/Memory/etc. The
route now also distinguishes "loading" from "couldn't start chat"
instead of showing "Starting chat..." for the error case.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: resolve chat agent via setup() so renamed CEOs work

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat): focus input when switching between agents/sessions
rawCommits.body:
The "don't steal focus when switching desktop chats" latch suppressed
auto-focus whenever the input wasn't already focused at the moment of
the switch. In practice that meant any sidebar click (which moves
focus to the clicked row) left the cursor stranded outside the input,
forcing a manual click before typing.

Re-arm focus on every thread reset so navigating between agents,
sessions, or fresh canvases drops the cursor straight into the chat
input on desktop. The focus effect's existing `isMobileLayout` guard
still prevents popping the on-screen keyboard on mobile.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: focus input when switching between agents/sessions

rawCommits.subject: fix(video): drop unused `name` field from GenerateVideoRequest
rawCommits.body:
The downstream `aura_protocol::GenerationRequest` has no `name` field,
so the value was deserialized and silently dropped. Remove it to clear
the dead_code warning; serde still ignores the unknown key sent by the
frontend, so behavior is unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): soften turn watchdog + non-terminal stream-lagged + env-tunable broadcast capacity
rawCommits.body:
Raise the chat-turn watchdog from a hard 30s/300s pair to env-tunable
defaults of 120s first-event / 30-min sliding idle, so long Opus
thinking + tool-use turns no longer trip a synthetic `turn_timeout`
mid-stream. Demote `stream_lagged` from a terminal SSE error to a
transient `progress: lagged` hint so a slow consumer no longer kills
the live turn. Raise the harness WS broadcast channel from 4096 to
16384 events and expose `AURA_HARNESS_BROADCAST_CAPACITY` so we can
tune backpressure without a rebuild.

Phase 1 of the agent-stream reliability plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: soften turn watchdog + non-terminal stream-lagged + env-tunable broadcast capacity

rawCommits.subject: fix(titlebar): vertically center EARN button label
rawCommits.body:
The label inherited the document line-height (~1.5), reserving phantom descender space that pushed the all-caps glyphs above the pill's flex center. Setting `line-height: 1` collapses the line box to glyph height so align-items: center lines up correctly.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(harness,chat): retry initial WS connect + client auto-retry on stream-dropped
rawCommits.body:
LocalHarness and SwarmHarness now retry the initial WebSocket connect
up to 3 times with exponential backoff (env-tunable via
AURA_HARNESS_CONNECT_ATTEMPTS / AURA_HARNESS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECS),
so a transient network blip on session open no longer fails the
chat. Capacity-exhausted (503/1013) and identity-preflight failures
short-circuit immediately and are never retried.

On the client, harness_ws_closed and harness_ws_read_error now
classify as the same recoverable streamDropped variant as
SSEIdleTimeoutError, and the chat hook auto-retries the last user
message up to 2 times with 1s/2s backoff. The harness picks up the
conversation from storage on each retry, so the user sees the
assistant turn resume after a "Reconnecting..." banner instead of
losing the message.

True mid-turn session resume remains blocked on session_resume
in aura-node and is called out in the ws_bridge TODO.

Phase 2 of the agent-stream reliability plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: retry initial WS connect + client auto-retry on stream-dropped

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): auto-fork chat sessions when context usage crosses threshold
rawCommits.body:
When AssistantMessageEnd.usage.context_utilization >= 0.80 (env
AURA_CHAT_AUTO_FORK_THRESHOLD), the persist task now flags the
storage session row as `rolled_over` and writes a rollover_summary
event with a one-paragraph summary of the conversation. The next
user send detects the flag in resolve_chat_session_with_pin, mints
a fresh session via SessionService::create_chat_followup_session
carrying summary_of_previous_context forward, evicts the stale
delegated harness session, and emits a `progress: forked_for_context`
SSE event so the chat UI updates `?session=` and shows a subtle
"Continued from previous chat" banner. The in-flight turn that
triggered the rollover still finalizes on the original session;
forking only affects the next user message.

Phase 3 of the agent-stream reliability plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: auto-fork chat sessions when context usage crosses threshold

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat): per-(partition,model) registry + DashMap + raise queue cap to 4 + narrow bare-agent busy guard
rawCommits.body:
Concurrency rework: the chat-session registry is now keyed on
(partition, model) and backed by DashMap, so two clients on the
same agent instance can run different models in parallel without
evicting each other. The per-partition turn queue cap rises from
2 to 4 (1 in-flight + 3 queued; env AURA_PARTITION_TURN_QUEUE).
The bare-agent route's automation busy guard is narrowed so a
loop on a sibling instance no longer blocks bare-agent chat.

After this phase a single user can have ~128 simultaneously active
turns process-wide spread across as many distinct agents / models
as they want, with no cross-agent serialization.

Phase 4 of the agent-stream reliability plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: per-(partition,model) registry + DashMap + raise queue cap to 4 + narrow bare-agent busy guard

rawCommits.subject: feat(stability): observability counters + /api/admin/health + client stream-close breadcrumbs
rawCommits.body:
Adds an in-process StabilityMetrics struct (lock-free AtomicU64
counters) covering the reliability work from phases 1-4: turns
started/completed, stream_stalled, turn_timeout, stream_lagged,
harness_ws_closed/read_error/protocol_mismatch, harness initial
connect retries, agent_busy_queue_full, auto_fork triggered/applied,
and client auto-retry on streamDropped. Surfaces a JSON snapshot at
/api/admin/health together with active chat-session and automaton
counts and the resolved env config.

Client-side, every stream close fires a structured `aura:stream-close`
CustomEvent breadcrumb and sets the `X-Aura-Client-Retry` request
header on Phase 2 auto-retries so the server counter is wired
end-to-end. No new external metrics dependency; everything reads
through the existing tracing + event infra.

Phase 5 (final phase) of the agent-stream reliability plan.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: fix(observability): guard process.env behind globalThis under browser-only tsconfig
rawCommits.body:
The Phase 5 stream-close breadcrumb (`isDevBuild`) referenced
`process.env.NODE_ENV` directly as a fallback when `import.meta.env.DEV`
is absent. The interface ships with a browser-only tsconfig that does
not include `@types/node`, so `tsc -b` (run by aura-os-desktop's
build.rs) fails with TS2591: "Cannot find name 'process'" and the whole
Tauri build aborts.

The fallback was always intended for Vitest's jsdom polyfill of
`process.env`. Reach it via `globalThis` so the runtime probe still
works while the static type universe stays browser-only — no
`@types/node` devDependency needed.

Verified `npm run build` is clean and the 4 stream-breadcrumbs vitest
cases still pass.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: guard process.env behind globalThis under browser-only tsconfig

rawCommits.subject: fix(agent-env): show agent workspace folder in hover card
rawCommits.body:
The local "File Path" row was reading `envInfo.cwd`, i.e. the
aura-os-server process's launch directory, regardless of which
agent/project the chat was bound to. That made the value misleading
whenever the agent's resolved workspace differed from the server CWD.

Wire the already-resolved `workspacePath` (from `useTerminalTarget`,
which honors `AgentInstance.workspace_path`,
`Agent.local_workspace_path`, and `Project.local_workspace_path`)
through `ChatInputBar` / `MobileChatInputBar` into `AgentEnvironment`
and rename the row to "Workspace Folder". The server CWD remains the
fallback for project-less chats so behavior is unchanged when no
workspace is known.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: show agent workspace folder in hover card

rawCommits.subject: fix(chat-stream): per-partition send-control for parallel chats
rawCommits.body:
Repair the dual UI breakage that surfaced when chatting with two agents in
the kept-mounted AgentChatPanel:

- Agent B's send no longer silently no-ops after switching from agent A
  mid-stream. The inFlight gate is now per-(projectId, agentInstanceId)
  via partition-send-control, so one partition's in-flight POST never
  blocks another's entry.

- Agent A's UI no longer freezes after the user switches away mid-stream.
  sendMessage now captures (partitionKey, partitionSetters, partitionRefs,
  agentInstanceId) at entry; the finally cleanup, the in-flight handler,
  and the auto-retry replay path all write to A's slot via captured
  setters regardless of which partition the panel is currently rendering.
  Final assistant bubble and isStreaming/sidekick spinner clearance now
  land on A's slot without requiring a refresh.

- Auto-retry timer is partition-bound: it captures the originating
  partition's identifiers and replays via api.sendEventStream against
  the captured (projectId, agentInstanceId) so a transient SSE drop on
  the previously-mounted agent recovers cleanly even if the user has
  since navigated to a different agent.

- useStreamCore useLayoutEffect cleanup no longer cancels in-flight
  RAF/flushTimeout when the entry is still streaming (treats kept-mounted
  prop change as a panel swap, not a true unmount).

New module: interface/src/hooks/use-chat-stream/partition-send-control.ts
holds per-partition send-control state, mirroring the per-key Zustand
stream store. clearPartitionSendControl wires into pruneStreamStore for
unified partition lifecycle.

Tests: interface/src/hooks/use-chat-stream/parallel-chats.test.ts covers
symptom 1 (B silent after switch), symptom 2 (A finalization on captured
partition), mid-stream switch with no second send, two-hook parallel
sanity, and auto-retry-after-switch.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

rawCommits.subject: feat(chat-app): cross-agent session inbox with per-row avatars
rawCommits.body:
Broaden the Chat app's left panel into a unified ChatGPT-style inbox
that spans every agent the user has chatted with (not just the
canonical CEO chat agent), shows the session's agent avatar on the
right of each row, eliminates the cross-bucket multi-select bug, and
swaps both the chat panel and the sidekick to follow the selected
session's agent.

- SessionsList now renders a single bucketed list of native <button>
  rows instead of one ZUI Explorer per date bucket. Each per-bucket
  Explorer kept its own provider/focus state, which made it possible
  for rows in different time-period sections to read as simultaneously
  highlighted. With a single parent-owned `effectiveSelectedSessionId`
  there is exactly one selected row across the entire surface.
- Added an optional `renderRowSuffix` prop so callers can paint custom
  right-side content per row. The Agents `ChatsTab` and projects
  `SessionList` keep their existing project-name suffix behavior;
  the chat-app passes a per-session `<Avatar>` resolved from each
  agent's project bindings.
- New `useChatAppSessions` hook merges `sessionsBySurface` across
  every agent and re-sorts via `sortSessionsDesc` (now exported from
  `sessions-list-store`).
- `ChatAppLeftPanel` fans out `loadAgentSessions(agentId)` across
  `useAgents()` and navigates to `/chat?agent&project&instance&session`
  so the route can mount the right chat panel before the merged
  session list has loaded.
- `ChatAppRoute` resolves the effective agent in URL > session > CEO
  fallback order and mirrors it into `useSelectedAgent()` so the
  shared `AgentInfoPanel` / `AgentSidekickTaskbar` automatically
  re-render the right profile/chats/skills/memory tabs for whichever
  agent owns the active conversation.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>
rawCommits.cleanSubject: cross-agent session inbox with per-row avatars

rendered.title: A standalone Chat app and a five-phase agent-stream reliability overhaul
rendered.intro: Today's nightly lands a brand-new ChatGPT-style Chat app at /chat alongside a top-to-bottom reliability rework of the agent streaming pipeline — softer watchdogs, automatic WS reconnects, context-aware session forking, parallel turns per model, and end-to-end observability. A handful of smaller polish fixes round out the chat surface across desktop and mobile.

entries.title: Video thumbnails in the Sidekick panel
entries.summary: AuraVideo's sidekick now previews real video frames instead of a generic icon.

items.text: Sidekick rows for videos render a still frame captured at the 0.5s mark via a media-fragment preload, with a Film icon as a graceful fallback when the frame can't be decoded.

entries.title: ChatGPT-style Chat app at /chat
entries.summary: A dedicated everyday-LLM app ships with its own route, sessions list, and fixes for the first paper cuts.

items.text: New top-level Chat app at /chat mounts a date-bucketed sessions list, the standard ChatPanel against the user's super-agent, and reuses the Agents app's AgentInfoPanel as a collapsed-by-default sidekick; the default model is seeded to aura-gpt-5-4-mini.

Accounts whose CEO agent had been renamed no longer get stuck on "Starting chat…" — the route now resolves the canonical chat agent through a cached api.superAgent.setup() call and distinguishes loading from an actual setup failure.

Switching between agents or sessions in the sidebar now drops the cursor straight into the chat input on desktop instead of leaving focus stranded on the clicked row; the mobile keyboard guard is preserved.

entries.title: Agent-stream reliability plan: phases 1–5
entries.summary: A coordinated five-phase rework hardens the chat streaming pipeline end-to-end, from watchdog timings to observability.

items.text: Phase 1 softens the chat-turn watchdog from a hard 30s/300s pair to env-tunable 120s first-event / 30-min sliding-idle defaults, demotes stream_lagged from a terminal SSE error to a transient progress hint, and quadruples the harness WS broadcast capacity to 16384 (tunable via AURA_HARNESS_BROADCAST_CAPACITY) so long Opus tool-use turns and slow consumers no longer kill live streams.

Phase 2 makes WS connects resilient: LocalHarness and SwarmHarness retry the initial connect up to 3 times with 500ms/1s/2s backoff, and the client now treats harness_ws_closed/read_error as recoverable streamDropped, auto-retrying the last user message twice behind a "Reconnecting…" banner instead of losing it.

Phase 3 introduces automatic session forking: once context_utilization crosses 0.80 (AURA_CHAT_AUTO_FORK_THRESHOLD), the next user send transparently mints a fresh session seeded with a rollover summary and the UI shows a subtle "Continued from previous chat" banner — no more hitting upstream context caps mid-conversation.

Phase 4 reworks chat concurrency: the session registry is now keyed on (partition, model) and backed by DashMap, the per-partition turn queue grows from 2 to 4, and the bare-agent busy guard is narrowed so a loop on a sibling instance no longer blocks bare-agent chat — enabling ~128 simultaneous turns per user across distinct agents and models.

Phase 5 wires up observability: a new lock-free StabilityMetrics struct tracks every reliability counter from phases 1–4 and exposes them as a JSON snapshot at /api/admin/health alongside active session counts and resolved env config; the client emits aura:stream-close breadcrumbs and sets X-Aura-Client-Retry on auto-retries so the server counter is wired end-to-end.

Follow-up fixes keep the EARN button label vertically centered in the titlebar, drop a dead `name` field from the video generation request to silence a dead_code warning, and guard the Phase 5 breadcrumb's process.env fallback behind globalThis so the browser-only tsconfig (and the Tauri desktop build) stays green.

entries.title: Parallel chats and a cross-agent inbox for /chat
entries.summary: The Chat app gains a unified cross-agent session list, and the streaming hook is rebuilt around per-partition state so two chats can run side by side.

items.text: Chat's left panel becomes a unified cross-agent inbox: SessionsList now renders a single bucketed list of native button rows (eliminating the cross-bucket multi-select bug), each row paints the session's agent avatar via a new renderRowSuffix prop, and selecting a session swaps both the chat panel and the sidekick to that agent's profile, chats, skills, and memory.

Chatting with two agents in a kept-mounted panel no longer breaks: a new per-(projectId, agentInstanceId) send-control module fixes Agent B silently no-op'ing after a mid-stream switch and Agent A's UI freezing on the final assistant bubble, with auto-retry timers now partition-bound so transient SSE drops recover cleanly even after the user navigates away.

The agent environment hover card now shows the chat's actual workspace folder — resolved from AgentInstance, Agent, or Project bindings via useTerminalTarget — instead of always falling back to the aura-os-server launch directory, and the row is relabeled "Workspace Folder" on both desktop and mobile.

highlights: New ChatGPT-style Chat app at /chat with cross-agent inbox
Five-phase agent-stream reliability plan shipped end-to-end
Auto-forking chat sessions when context fills up
Parallel chats per (agent, model) with per-partition send control
